feed.title: 一孔录 · Reading the classics word by word
feed.subtitle: Every line Yikonglu has read aloud can be checked here.

entry.title: 7.10 用之则行，舍之则藏
entry.summary: 子谓颜渊曰：用之则行，舍之则藏；唯我与尔有是夫。子路曰：子行三军，则谁与？子曰：暴虎冯河，死而无悔者，吾不与也。必也，临事而惧，好谋而成者也。 —— 出来做不为贪位，收起来不为只顾自己，心里没有非用不可的念头才做得到；子路以勇自负，孔子要的是遇事知怕、肯谋划、能办成的人。今例：登山队出发前一晚领队一条条问怎么撤，问得最细的人最敢上山。

entry.title: 7.9 子食于有丧者之侧（是日哭则不歌）
entry.summary: 子食于有丧者之侧，未尝饱也。子于是日哭，则不歌。 —— 不是守规矩，是心里真哀伤：挨着办丧事的人吃不出味道，吊丧哭过的那天唱不出来。今例：参加完葬礼开车回家，音乐一响伸手就关了。

entry.title: 7.8 不愤不启，不悱不发
entry.summary: 子曰：不愤不启，不悱不发。举一隅不以三隅反，则不复也。 —— 上一集谁来都教，这一章讲怎么教：等学的人急到想通想说的时候再点；举一角推不出三角，就先不往下讲。今例：孩子一道题卡半小时，妈妈不递答案，只问卡在哪一步。

entry.title: 7.7 自行束脩以上
entry.summary: 子曰：自行束脩以上，吾未尝无诲焉。 —— 束脩是最薄的见面礼，重点不在学费，在“来学”：肯带着礼主动来，孔子没有不教的；不来，没有上门去教的礼。今例：社区免费夜校门一直开着，带个本子来就够。

entry.title: 7.6 志于道，据于德，依于仁，游于艺
entry.summary: 子曰：志于道，据于德，依于仁，游于艺。 —— 四步有先后轻重：先立志，再守得住，再不离仁，余力在六艺里游，游也不是闲玩，是让心有处安放。今例：白天上班，晚上练一个钟头字，字不当饭吃，人不会散。

entry.title: 7.5 甚矣吾衰也
entry.summary: 子曰：甚矣吾衰也！久矣吾不复梦见周公！ —— 梦不见周公，不是心不向道了，是身子做不动、行道之心也随之歇了；守道的心不分老少，行道的身会老。今例：退休老工程师讲图纸眉飞色舞，说一句“工地我是跑不动了”。

entry.title: 7.4 子之燕居
entry.summary: 子之燕居，申申如也，夭夭如也。 —— 不是孔子的话，是弟子记的样子：闲在家里身子舒展、脸色和悦，不端着也不瘫着。今例：周末在家笑着给阳台的花浇水。

entry.title: 7.3 德之不修
entry.summary: 子曰：德之不脩，学之不讲，闻义不能徙，不善不能改，是吾忧也。 —— 四件都是天天要做的功夫，做不到就忧，圣人尚且如此，何况一般人。今例：说好不熬夜又拿起手机，真把手机放远了才算改。

entry.title: 7.2 默而识之
entry.summary: 子曰：默而识之，学而不厌，诲人不倦，何有于我哉？ —— 默记在心、学不嫌够、教不嫌累，本不算圣人的顶点，孔子还说自己没做到，是谦上加谦。今例：夜里还在批作业的老师，被夸时说自己还差得远。

entry.title: 7.1 述而不作
entry.summary: 子曰：述而不作，信而好古，窃比于我老彭。 —— 孔子删诗书、定礼乐，自认只是传旧；德越高心越低，说的是真心，不是客套。可当时作者已多，把它们收拢折中，功劳反比创作大。今例：老字号学徒照师傅的老方子一步步做，方子才没断。

entry.title: 6.28 博施济众（能近取譬）
entry.summary: 子贡曰：如有博施于民而能济众，何如？可谓仁乎？子曰：何事于仁？必也圣乎！尧舜其犹病诸！夫仁者，己欲立而立人，己欲达而达人。能近取譬，可谓仁之方也已。 —— 博施济众连尧舜都觉得做不全，拿它求仁越求越远；仁从近处下手，己欲立而立人。今例：救天下人谁也够不着，地铁里给站不稳的老先生让个座是够得着的。

entry.title: 6.27 中庸之为德
entry.summary: 子曰：中庸之为德也，其至矣乎！民鲜久矣。 —— 不过头也不够不着，又天天不变，所以难；难在长久。今例：街角小面馆三十年准点开门，汤的咸淡没变过。

entry.title: 6.26 子见南子
entry.summary: 子见南子，子路不说。夫子矢之曰：予所否者，天厌之！天厌之！ —— 按礼该见就见，对方不好与己无干；子路一时想不透，孔子才连誓两遍，叫他先信再想。今例：公事上该见的人名声不好，照规矩见，自己守得住，闲话先由它去。

entry.title: 6.25 博学于文，约之以礼
entry.summary: 子曰：君子博学于文，约之以礼，亦可以弗畔矣夫！ —— 学要广，守要简；只博不约就漫成一片没边际。今例：收藏夹里存了几百节课，哪一节都没看完。

entry.title: 6.24 井有仁焉
entry.summary: 宰我问曰：仁者，虽告之曰：井有仁焉，其从之也？子曰：何为其然也？君子可逝也，不可陷也；可欺也，不可罔也。 —— 仁者急着救人，但站在井上才救得了人；合情理的话能骗他去井边，不合理的事蒙不住他。今例：电话里说家人出事要马上转账，她挂了电话先打给家里人。

entry.title: 6.23 觚不觚
entry.summary: 子曰：觚不觚，觚哉！觚哉！ —— 名还在、样子没了，就不算那个东西；说的是器，指的是君臣各失其道。今例：一把叫“椅子”的东西，好看却没法坐。

entry.title: 6.22 齐一变至于鲁
entry.summary: 子曰：齐一变，至于鲁；鲁一变，至于道。 —— 强弱看的是眼前，离道远近看的是风俗底子；鲁只要把荒废的修起来，齐得先改掉图功利的习气。今例：门口喇叭喊打折排长队，对面老店不吆喝、称秤一两不少。

entry.title: 6.21 知者乐水，仁者乐山
entry.summary: 子曰：知者乐水，仁者乐山。知者动，仁者静。知者乐，仁者寿。 —— 聪明人通达事理，像水流来流去不卡住；厚道人安于义理，像山厚重不挪动。动而不拘所以乐，静而有常所以寿。今例：一个爱沿江跑，一个爱在山亭坐一下午。

entry.title: 6.20 Did Confucius believe in spirits?
entry.summary: 樊迟问知。子曰：务民之义，敬鬼神而远之，可谓知矣。问仁。曰：仁者先难而后获，可谓仁矣。 —— The question is not belief or disbelief, but revering and keeping at a distance: first do fully what human affairs require, revere the spirits without petitioning them; in action, the hard part first and the gain after, without reckoning the benefit in advance.

entry.title: 6.19 Was Confucius looking down on people?
entry.summary: 子曰：中人以上，可以语上也；中人以下，不可以语上也。 —— This is not ranking people, but fitting words to the listener: speak too high and the listener cannot catch it, and harm is done. Teach according to capacity, and climb step by step.

entry.title: 6.18 Knowing, liking, delighting: what's the difference?
entry.summary: 子曰：知之者不如好之者，好之者不如乐之者。 —— Knowing there is this bowl of rice, loving to eat it, and having eaten your fill and being at ease: three levels. The difference is not how much you know, but whether you have actually gained it.

entry.title: 6.17 Don't crooked people live perfectly well too?
entry.summary: 子曰：人之生也直，罔之生也幸而免。 —— People are meant to live upright; the crooked are alive too, not because they deserve it but because they have got away with it by luck.

entry.title: 6.16 Too rough or too polished: which would Confucius prefer?
entry.summary: 子曰：质胜文则野，文胜质则史。文质彬彬，然后君子。 —— Too much plainness is crude, too much ornament is hollow; only the two in balance make a gentleman. If one must lean, better lean plain: with the base intact, refinement can be added; with the base gone, refinement has nowhere to go.

entry.title: 6.15 Everyone goes out by the door: why not by the right way?
entry.summary: 子曰：谁能出不由户？何莫由斯道也？ —— Everyone knows to leave by the door rather than climb the wall; the right road in life lies right in front of us, yet people will not take it. It is not that the Way is far from them; they have wandered away themselves.

entry.title: 6.14 Without a glib tongue or good looks, can one escape trouble?
entry.summary: 子曰：不有祝𬶍之佞而有宋朝之美，难乎免于今之世矣！ —— This is not advice to cultivate eloquence and looks; it is a lament for the times: when the world values only a sweet tongue and a pretty face, honest people can hardly escape harm.

entry.title: 6.13 He covered the retreat: why wouldn't he admit it?
entry.summary: 子曰：孟之反不伐，奔而殿。将入门，策其马，曰：非敢后也，马不进也。 —— Holding the rear against the enemy in a rout is great merit, yet as they neared the city gate he whipped his horse and said, “It wasn't that I dared to stay behind; the horse wouldn't go.” Passing the credit to his horse shows a heart with no wish to rise above others.

entry.title: 6.12 Not taking shortcuts: is that talent?
entry.summary: 子游为武城宰。子曰：女得人焉尔乎？曰：有澹台灭明者，行不由径。非公事，未尝至于偃之室也。 —— He never cut through by-paths and never came to the official's door without public business. Someone who holds firm in small things can be relied on in large ones; Ziyou saw that too when judging people.

entry.title: 6.11 Both are scholars: where is the difference?
entry.summary: 子谓子夏曰：女为君子儒，无为小人儒。 —— Studying the same books, one who learns to make something of himself is a gentleman scholar; one who learns to be seen and to gain advantage is a petty scholar. Profit is not only money; reputation counts too.

entry.title: 6.10 He said he lacked the strength: why didn't Confucius believe him?
entry.summary: 冉求曰：非不说子之道，力不足也。子曰：力不足者，中道而废。今女画。 —— Someone truly lacking strength collapses halfway along the road; Ran Qiu drew a line on the ground before setting out. It is not that he cannot, but that he will not.

entry.title: 6.9 So poor, what was Yan Hui happy about?
entry.summary: 子曰：贤哉，回也！一箪食，一瓢饮，在陋巷。人不堪其忧，回也不改其乐。贤哉，回也！ —— What he enjoyed was not poverty, but a joy that poverty could not change. Zhu Xi would rather not spell it out, leaving readers to find for themselves what lies in the word “其”.

entry.title: 6.8 Why did Confucius hold his dying student's hand through the window?
entry.summary: 伯牛有疾，子问之，自牖执其手，曰：亡之，命矣夫！斯人也而有斯疾也！斯人也而有斯疾也！ —— Boniu's family moved the sickbed under the south window, as for a ruler's visit; Confucius did not dare accept that honour, so he did not enter and held his hand through the window in farewell. “That such a man should have such an illness” is said twice: grief that such a person should suffer such a disease, laid at the door of fate.

entry.title: 6.7 Offered an office, why would he flee?
entry.summary: 季氏使闵子骞为费宰。闵子骞曰：善为我辞焉。如有复我者，则吾必在汶上矣。 —— He would not become the Ji family's retainer, yet he asked the messenger to decline kindly for him, and if they came again he would cross the river to Qi. Neither defying them head-on nor giving in: too hard invites disaster, too soft invites disgrace.

entry.title: 6.6 Is a single quality enough to take office?
entry.summary: 季康子问：仲由可使从政也与？子曰：由也果，于从政乎何有？曰：赐也，可使从政也与？曰：赐也达，于从政乎何有？曰：求也，可使从政也与？曰：求也艺，于从政乎何有？ —— Zilu is decisive, Zigong perceptive, Ran Qiu many-skilled: each has one strength and so can be employed. Using people means taking what they are good at.

entry.title: 6.5 Where did Yan Hui differ from the others?
entry.summary: 子曰：回也，其心三月不违仁，其余则日月至焉而已矣。 —— Yan Hui's humaneness is like a host living at home who now and then steps out; the others' is like a guest who drops by now and then. The difference lies in how long it lasts, not in whether it is there.

entry.title: 6.4 Can someone of bad background be employed?
entry.summary: 子谓仲弓曰：犁牛之子骍且角，虽欲勿用，山川其舍诸？ —— A calf of a brindled plough-ox, pure red with well-formed horns: even if people will not sacrifice it because of its origin, the spirits of hills and rivers will not reject it. A father's badness cannot cancel a son's goodness; Zhu Xi notes specifically that this speaks about Zhonggong, not to his face.

entry.title: 6.3 Why did Confucius give one man little grain and another a lot?
entry.summary: 子华使于齐，冉子为其母请粟。子曰：与之釜。请益。曰：与之庾。冉子与之粟五秉。子曰：赤之适齐也，乘肥马，衣轻裘。吾闻之也，君子周急不继富。原思为之宰，与之粟九百，辞。子曰：毋！以与尔邻里乡党乎！ —— How much to give depends not on favour but on what is right. Zihua's family rode fat horses and wore light furs, not in need, so he gave only a little, refusing to add to the rich; Yuan Si's salary was owed by his post, and refusing it would be wrong, so any excess should go to his neighbours. One case is “help the needy, not the rich”; the other is “a regular salary should not be declined”.

entry.title: 6.2 Why is Confucius' “love of learning” not about reading a lot?
entry.summary: 哀公问：弟子孰为好学？孔子对曰：有颜回者好学，不迁怒，不贰过。不幸短命死矣！今也则亡，未闻好学者也。 —— Love of learning lies in governing one's feelings: not shifting anger onto others, not making the same mistake twice. Today: scolded at work, you still come home, crouch down, and tie your child's shoelaces properly.

entry.title: 6.1 Why can one's affairs be simple but not one's heart?
entry.summary: 子曰：雍也可使南面。仲弓问子桑伯子。子曰：可也简。仲弓曰：居敬而行简，以临其民，不亦可乎？居简而行简，无乃大简乎？子曰：雍之言然。 —— With a settled heart and respect in everything, affairs become simple of themselves; aiming first at ease and letting yourself off too is too simple. Today: in the team with the fewest rules, the person in charge is the most punctual and best organised of all.

entry.title: 5.27 The one thing Confucius claimed to have more of
entry.summary: 子曰：十室之邑，必有忠信如丘者焉，不如丘之好学也。 —— Loyalty and trust are the base, found everywhere; love of learning is effort, and rare. Confucius does not boast of innate knowledge, only of loving to learn, to encourage others. The Gongye Chang book ends here. Today: honest, reliable people are everywhere; people still going to night school at sixty are few.

entry.title: 5.26 Why is it so hard to see one's own faults?
entry.summary: 子曰：已矣乎！吾未见能见其过而内自讼者也。 —— Two levels: knowing one's fault is already rare; knowing it and blaming oneself inwardly is rarer still; only self-arraignment leads to thorough change. Confucius' sigh of “never seen” is a warning to learners. Today: she misreported a figure in a meeting and nobody noticed, and after the meeting she messaged everyone to correct it.

entry.title: 5.25 Why was Confucius' wish greater than Zilu's and Yan Yuan's?
entry.summary: 颜渊、季路侍。子曰：盍各言尔志？子路曰：愿车马、衣轻裘，与朋友共。敝之而无憾。颜渊曰：愿无伐善，无施劳。子路曰：愿闻子之志。子曰：老者安之，朋友信之，少者怀之。 —— All three share with others, differing in scale: Zilu shares carriage and horses with friends, Yan Yuan does not boast or show off, Confucius lets each find their place, like heaven and earth nurturing without a trace. Today: the auntie in the housing block whom the elderly trust with their keys and to whose door the children run first after school.

entry.title: 5.24 Why did Confucius find excessive politeness shameful?
entry.summary: 子曰：巧言、令色、足恭，左丘明耻之，丘亦耻之。匿怨而友其人，左丘明耻之，丘亦耻之。 —— Both shames are a gap between inside and outside: sweet words, smiles and excessive courtesy to curry favour; befriending someone while nursing a grudge is pretence. Xie says it is worse than theft, because the heart is not upright. Today: holding a grudge, yet being the first at the table to raise a glass to him.

entry.title: 5.23 Why is borrowing something for a neighbour not upright?
entry.summary: 子曰：孰谓微生高直？或乞醯焉，乞诸其邻而与之。 —— Saying “I don't have any” is upright; passing off a borrowed thing as your own is bending to please — a small matter, but Master Cheng says what it harms is uprightness itself. Today: a colleague asks for a charging cable, you borrow one from the next desk and say “Here, use mine.”

entry.title: 5.22 Bo Yi and Shu Qi were so aloof — why did no one resent them?
entry.summary: 子曰：伯夷、叔齐不念旧恶，怨是用希。 —— So fastidious they seemed to tolerate no one, yet they stopped once a person changed, so few resented them; the measure of the pure is not keeping old accounts. Today: the neighbour you once quarrelled with apologised, and you still nod to each other on the stairs.

entry.title: 5.21 After so many years of travel, what did Confucius go home to do?
entry.summary: 子在陈曰：归与！归与！吾党之小子狂简，斐然成章，不知所以裁之。 —— He turns from practising the Way to transmitting it; ambitious young men can advance in the Way, but risk overshooting, so he goes home to trim them. Today: a new hire's proposal has eight good ideas in ten pages, and still needs someone to help cut it down.

entry.title: 5.20 Why is this “foolishness” harder to learn than cleverness?
entry.summary: 子曰：寗武子邦有道则知，邦无道则愚。其知可及也，其愚不可及也。 —— The “foolishness” is taking on what every clever person avoids, while still keeping himself safe and saving his lord; Master Cheng's mention of Bi Gan shows it is not simply feigning stupidity. Today: the year the company hit trouble everyone left, and she stayed to sort out the bad books.

entry.title: 5.19 Why is thinking twice enough?
entry.summary: 季文子三思而后行。子闻之，曰：再，斯可矣。 —— By the second time it is already clear; by the third, self-interest creeps in. Today: a contract is clear after two readings; by the fourth, you start finding faults that aren't faults.

entry.title: 5.18 Not even this counts as ren?
entry.summary: 子张问曰：令尹子文三仕为令尹，无喜色；三已之，无愠色。旧令尹之政，必以告新令尹。何如？子曰：忠矣。曰：仁矣乎？曰：未知，焉得仁？崔子弑齐君，陈文子有马十乘，弃而违之。至于他邦，则曰：犹吾大夫崔子也。违之。之一邦，则又曰：犹吾大夫崔子也。违之。何如？子曰：清矣。曰：仁矣乎？曰：未知。焉得仁？ —— Loyalty and purity are single virtues; ren asks whether one fully accords with principle and truly has no selfish mind. Trusting small things to vouch for great ones was Zizhang's fault. Today: leaving a job with a clean handover, even the password book left behind, is loyalty to duty — no more than that yet.

entry.title: 5.17 Was Zang Wenzhong really clever?
entry.summary: 子曰：臧文仲居蔡，山节藻棁，何如其知也？ —— Not putting his mind to what the people needed, and courting spirits instead, does not count as wisdom. Today: business is slow, and instead of asking customers, the owner spends a fortune turning the shop door to face another way.

entry.title: 5.16 Is it more polite not to stand on ceremony with old friends?
entry.summary: 子曰：晏平仲善与人交，久而敬之。 —— Respect fading with time is the usual course; keeping it is what “good at associating with others” means. Today: after five years sharing a flat, a roommate still knocks before borrowing your charger.
